newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Nov real earnings rose 1.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Nov real earnings rose 1.0 pct.

text.p: Average weekly earnings of U.S. workers, after adjusting for inflation and seasonal factors, rose 1.0 percent in November, the Labor Department said Thursday.
The November increase followed a 1.5 percent drop in October real average weekly earnings.

The November rise stems from a 0.6 percent rise in average weekly hours, a 0.8 percent increase in average hourly earnings and a 0.3 percent rise in the Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers.
Real average weekly earnings in November were up 0.2 percent from November last year, the department said.

In constant 1982 dollars, weekly earnings for non-supervisory private workers outside the farm sector averaged a seasonally adjusted $257.09 in November, versus $254.47 in October and $255.91 in November 1995.
In current dollars, weekly earnings averaged a seasonally adjusted $413.66 in November, compared with $408.17 in October and $398.70 in November last year.
